cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet is passing along a message from the LORD about prophets who claim to speak for Him. And the LORD opens with a question. “Am I only a God nearby,” declares the LORD, “and not a God far away?”

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says a man can hide in secret places where He cannot see him.

cards.text: Nope, the LORD fills the heavens and the earth. Friend, I once tried to hide behind a rolling pin. With THIS mustache. Hiding from the LORD works out even worse.
Then the LORD says He has heard what the prophets are saying, the ones who prophesy lies in His name.

cards.question: The prophets who prophesy lies in the LORD's name keep announcing they had something. What is it?

cards.text: Their big line is “I had a dream! I had a dream!” TWICE, friend, like the buddy who texts you his whole dream at six in the morning before you've even found your glasses.

cards.question: The LORD asks how long this will go on. He says these prophets' dreams come out of their own ___.

cards.text: These prophets tell their dreams to one another. And the LORD says what they suppose all those dreams will do to His people.

cards.question: True or false: The prophets suppose their dreams will make the LORD's people forget His name.
The LORD says the people's fathers forgot His name the same way, through the worship of ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD draws a line: let the one with a dream retell it, but let the one with His word speak it truthfully. And He asks what straw is compared to grain.

cards.question: True or false: In the LORD's picture of straw and grain, His word is the straw.

cards.text: His word is the grain, friend. Those dreams? A PHOTO of a cookie. Real nice to look at, and you will NOT be putting it in a cookie box.
Then the LORD asks another question. “Is not My word like fire,” declares the LORD, “and like a hammer that smashes a rock?”

cards.question: The LORD says His word is like fire and like a hammer that smashes a rock. What do those pictures show about His word?

cards.text: Then the LORD says He is against the prophets, and He spells out exactly which ones. First up, the prophets with words they attribute to Him.

cards.question: Where do these prophets get the words they say came from the LORD?

answers.text: They steal them from one another
They copy them from old scrolls
They buy them from the priests

cards.text: Next, the prophets who wag their own tongues and proclaim, “The LORD declares it.” That's the coworker who sticks “the boss said” on the end of EVERY sentence. “Copier's jammed, the boss said.” “Nice weather, the boss said.”

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says He sent the prophets with false dreams, but they changed His message along the way.
The LORD says these prophets lead His people astray with reckless lies. How much do they benefit His people?

cards.text: Now the LORD takes on a question. When this people or a prophet or priest asks, “What is the burden of the LORD?” there's an answer they're to be given.

cards.question: When someone asks what the burden of the LORD is, the answer starts with “What burden?” What does the LORD then say He will do?

cards.text: Then there's the prophet or priest or anyone who claims, “This is the burden of the LORD,” and the LORD has something to say about that man.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says He will punish the man who claims “This is the burden of the LORD,” and his household too.
Instead of claiming “This is the burden of the LORD,” what does the LORD say each man should ask his friend and his brother?

cards.text: Then the LORD tells them to refer no more to the burden of the LORD. And He gives the reason.

cards.question: Why does the LORD tell the people to refer no more to the burden of the LORD?

answers.text: They twist the words of the living God
They say the phrase far too often
Only the priests may say the phrase

cards.text: The LORD says “each man’s word becomes the burden,” and friend, I know how that goes. Give me ONE week of scribbling my own recipes on cards and signing them with the name of Mother Miller, the lady whose kitchen I baked in for years, and nobody would know what she ACTUALLY said.
Same goes when the people go to a prophet. They're to ask, “What has the LORD answered you?” and “What has the LORD spoken?”

But if anyone claims “This is the burden of the LORD” anyway, the LORD says He specifically told them not to make this claim. Friend, “specifically told you not to” is the voice in my head every time the timer says not yet and I open the oven ANYWAY.

cards.question: Because they made the claim He told them not to make, what does the LORD say He will surely do?

answers.text: Forget them and cast them out

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says the city He gave to them and their fathers would be cast out of His presence along with them.
The LORD says the shame and humiliation He brings on them will last ___.

findings.problem: The opening card identifies Jeremiah and the LORD and introduces the message about the false prophets, but it never says to whom the message is being spoken.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: This story card runs to four sentences: the statement about the LORD filling heaven and earth, the rolling-pin sentence, 'With THIS mustache.' and the final sentence about hiding from the LORD. Only the opening card may exceed two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards points to Baal rather than Dagon or Molech. The baker can only guess an unseen name, so the blank does not test a meaning that can be reasoned out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'His word is the grain, friend.', 'Those dreams?', 'A PHOTO of a cookie.' and the final cookie-box sentence. It exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: the statement about the prophets, the coworker comparison, and the two example sentences beginning 'Copier's jammed' and 'Nice weather'. It exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question does not identify who 'they' are or what 'the claim' is. Both depend on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen; the question should name the people and the claim, 'This is the burden of the LORD.'

rule.text: The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: The earlier cards provide no basis for choosing how long the shame and humiliation will last. Until verse 40 is revealed, a baker cannot reason out 'forever' rather than 'a season' or 'a generation'.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
